title: Large language models for OCR in cultural heritage: a comparative study on Slovene Folkloristic texts
summary: Benchmarks six OCR routes - Tesseract alone, Tesseract with LLM post-correction, direct transcription by a general multimodal LLM, LLaMA 4 Maverick, Nanonets OCR-3, and Qwen-VL-OCR - against manually aligned ground truth on two Slovene heritage collections: uniformly typewritten folklore manuscripts and a visually heterogeneous children's magazine. Document-oriented and direct multimodal systems win on the clean typewritten material, while accuracy on the magazine tracks layout complexity more than model choice, so the authors argue for content-aware routing between strategies instead of one fixed pipeline. Scoring uses CER and WER plus sequence-based measures, which is the level of granularity needed to see whether errors are structural or character-level.
igbo_relevance: The undigitised Igbo print archive - mission-era orthographies, dense sub-dot and tone diacritics, mixed layouts - is the same problem class, and this gives both a shortlist of OCR routes to try first and a warning that per-collection CER on diacritic-bearing vowels, not a single corpus-level number, is what decides whether the text is usable as training data.

title: Seeking commonality while preserving diversity: A differential dual-path MoE solution for Multilingual Neural Machine Translation
summary: Proposes a mixture-of-experts architecture for multilingual NMT built around two differentiated paths, one carrying structure shared across languages and one reserved for language-specific capacity, aimed squarely at the interference-versus-sharing tradeoff that governs many-to-many translation quality. OpenAlex has not indexed an abstract for this record, so it is logged as a lead: the routing scheme, expert budget, and language set still have to be read off the paper. It is tracked anyway because the shared/specific split is a core-task method question rather than a resource release.
igbo_relevance: Whether a low-resource language gains from or is drowned out by its high-resource neighbours in a massively multilingual model like NLLB-200 is decided by exactly this allocation, so the paper is a direct read on how to give Igbo dedicated capacity without losing cross-lingual transfer.

title: Normal-Anchored First-Order Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning based Whisper Fine-Tuning for Enhancing Fairness of Cleft Lip and Palate Speech Recognition
summary: Adapts Whisper to cleft lip and palate speech with a first-order meta-learning scheme in which plentiful typical speech anchors the inner loop while severity-stratified pathological speech drives the outer loop, so the objective optimises for robustness after adaptation rather than fit to whichever condition dominates the training mix. The authors ablate which Whisper encoder layers to unfreeze (0-5, 4-11, 6-11, 8-11) alongside decoder and projection-head tuning on two clinical corpora, and report that anchoring on typical speech alone is not sufficient - severe cases still degrade badly, with word error rates above 50% where typical speech sits near 4%. The honest reporting of that residual gap is more useful than the headline averages.
igbo_relevance: Igbo ASR faces the same data shape - one large anchor of abundant speech plus a small, internally heterogeneous target set spanning dialects and accents - so both the anchored meta-learning objective and the encoder-layer ablation are worth replicating directly when fine-tuning Whisper on the little transcribed Igbo audio that exists.

title: Axiveri/NaijaVox-2.0
summary: A fine-tune of openai/whisper-large-v3 released as a single checkpoint covering the five speech varieties that dominate Nigerian audio - Igbo, Yoruba, Hausa, Nigerian English, and Nigerian Pidgin - rather than one model per language, which is the pragmatic choice when each language contributes only a few hours of transcribed speech. Roughly a thousand downloads is meaningful traction for this corner of the hub. The model card was not reachable from this environment, so the training corpus, per-language hour counts, and any reported error rates remain unverified and are the first thing to check.
igbo_relevance: This is one of very few publicly downloadable ASR checkpoints that claims Igbo coverage at all, so it is worth benchmarking as a baseline before any in-house Whisper fine-tune - with the caveat that Nigerian multilingual releases are routinely dominated by English and Pidgin data, making a held-out Igbo-only WER (and a check on whether tone diacritics survive in the transcripts) the decisive test.

title: Large Language Models for Low-Resource Languages: A Conceptual Framework for an Electronic Explanatory Dictionary of the Tajik Language
summary: Proposes an architecture for building a monolingual explanatory dictionary with LLMs in the loop, decomposed into morphological analysis, lemmatisation, semantic clustering, and generation of the entries themselves, on top of a prior survey of what linguistic, statistical, and corpus resources for Tajik already exist. Two design commitments are argued rather than assumed: subword tokenisation chosen against the language's agglutinative morphology and high surface variability, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning as the adaptation strategy given almost no annotated data. It is explicitly a conceptual framework - no implementation, ablation, or evaluation is reported, so it offers a blueprint and a rationale, not evidence.
igbo_relevance: Igbo has no machine-readable explanatory dictionary of comparable scope, and this module decomposition is a reusable plan for assembling one from existing scattered lexicographic material - kept as a borderline case, since the transfer is in the pipeline design and the morphology-driven tokenisation argument rather than in any validated result.

title: Decolonizing Linguistic Policies in Automated Speech Recognition: A Framework for Cross-Culturally Competent Speech AI
summary: Argues that the persistent failure of ASR on low-resource, Indigenous, and non-standard varieties is better read as de facto language policy than as a series of isolated engineering bugs, tracing how corpus composition, choice of metric, and model priors jointly decide which speakers a system can hear. The contribution is conceptual apparatus: a three-part harm taxonomy (misrecognition, misalignment, mistrust) and a seven-layer account of the situational factors, from phonology up to institutional setting, that govern who a voice interface serves. It closes with a participatory design protocol and a minimum audit checklist that places speaker communities as evaluators and governance partners rather than data sources. No systems are built or benchmarked, so it is a framework to apply, not evidence about any particular model.
igbo_relevance: The minimum audit protocol is directly usable as a checklist for this project's ASR evaluation - it argues for per-dialect and per-accent error reporting with community sign-off on the test set, which is exactly what a single Nigerian-aggregate WER hides when Igbo contributes a small slice of the audio.

title: MameLoshnLM: Yiddish Language Model and Evaluation Benchmark
summary: Continues pretraining Llama 3.1 8B on Oytser, a purpose-built Yiddish corpus combining web-native text with literary material, and evaluates it on Kashes, a multi-task benchmark spanning translation, linguistic analysis, information extraction, and language understanding. The diagnosis is more valuable than the checkpoint: the authors show that the Yiddish portions of existing multilingual corpora are heavily polluted with machine-translated and language-misclassified text, so scale on web data buys very little, and they demonstrate that their model's advantage over same-size open baselines concentrates in the lexical and morphological patterns that actually define the language rather than in aggregate scores.
igbo_relevance: Igbo's slice of mC4/CC-100-style corpora suffers the same machine-translation contamination and language-ID misclassification, and this paper supplies both the audit that exposes it and a curate-then-continue-pretrain recipe at a scale one lab can afford - the contamination check is worth running on any Igbo web dump before it is used for pretraining.

title: Bangla Regional Dialect-to-Standard Bangla Parallel Corpus for Dialect Bias Evaluation
summary: A four-way parallel corpus of 15,376 dialect-to-Standard-Bangla sentence pairs spanning Barishali, Chittagonian, Sylheti, and Noakhali, assembled by merging four existing releases and closing the Noakhali gap with 1,807 sentences translated by native speakers and independently checked. The transferable part is the splitting protocol: the 3,844 underlying meanings are assigned to train/dev/test first and only then expanded into dialect pairs, so no meaning straddles a split. The authors also report the diagnostic that undercuts their own benchmark - 99.8% of test targets still appear in training through a sibling dialect - which bounds how much a strong score on it can mean.
igbo_relevance: Kept for the evaluation design rather than the data, since Igbo dialect normalisation across Owerri, Onitsha, and Central Igbo hits precisely this leakage trap when the same meaning is elicited in several varieties; the meaning-first split and the sibling-overlap diagnostic are the two things to adopt before reporting any Igbo dialect-normalisation result.

title: IWAC Sentiment Analysis Visualization
summary: Releases three-way LLM sentiment annotations over the Islam West Africa Collection - 12,287 francophone press articles from Benin, Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire, Niger, and Togo published between 1961 and 2025 - together with a SvelteKit dashboard for exploring them. GPT-5 mini, Gemini 3 Flash, and Ministral 3 14B each labelled every article on polarity, subjectivity, and how central Islam and Muslims are to the piece, and the interface surfaces per-model distributions alongside pairwise agreement including weighted Cohen's kappa, with geographic and temporal slices and CSV export. The design choice worth borrowing is the arbitration layer: rather than treating model disagreement as noise, blind judgements by a fourth model decide which annotation better fits the source text.
igbo_relevance: Igbo sentiment work has no gold-annotated corpus at anything like this scale, and this is an inspectable end-to-end protocol for building one by multi-model annotation with kappa reporting and blind arbitration - the reported agreement levels also give a realistic prior for how far LLM labels on African-context text can be trusted before human adjudication is unavoidable.

title: IWAC AI Pipelines
summary: A code release (not a data or model release) of the Python pipelines behind the Islam West Africa Collection, wiring LLMs into archive curation end to end: OCR extraction and post-correction, summarisation, named-entity recognition with reconciliation against authority files, audio and video transcription, handwritten text recognition, and sentiment analysis, with every result written back into an Omeka S repository. It is engineering rather than research - no benchmark or ablation is reported - but it is one of the few published, runnable examples of the whole chain from scanned or recorded Africa-context material through to a queryable collection. The authority-reconciliation step in the NER stage is what separates it from a generic prompt-and-parse script.
igbo_relevance: The Igbo digitisation backlog needs precisely this chain - OCR post-correction, ASR transcription, then NER over the output - so this supplies a working reference implementation and a storage pattern, letting effort go into the Igbo-specific pieces (diacritic-aware OCR correction, an Igbo gazetteer for the reconciliation step) instead of re-plumbing the pipeline.

title: AfriSpeech/african-speech-ipa
summary: A new release from the AfriSpeech group pairing African-language text with IPA phonemic transcription, between 100k and 1M rows in parquet. The catalogue metadata carries a text modality tag and no audio tag, so despite the name this looks like a pronunciation lexicon or grapheme-to-phoneme resource rather than a speech corpus, which if true makes it more reusable than an audio release. The card was not reachable from this environment, so the language inventory, the licence, and above all whether the IPA was produced by human phonetic annotation or by an automatic G2P remain unverified.
igbo_relevance: A pan-African IPA layer is the missing piece for an Igbo TTS front-end and for phoneme-based ASR that pools audio across languages, so the first check is whether Igbo appears at all and, if it does, whether the transcription encodes tone (two level tones plus downstep) or silently strips it, since an atonal IPA layer would be close to useless for Igbo synthesis.

title: SilencioNetwork/igbo-speech
summary: A small crowdsourced monolingual Igbo speech corpus, fewer than 1,000 clips in audiofolder layout with paired transcripts, tagged for both ASR and TTS and released under CC-BY-NC-4.0. Both the audio and the annotations are marked crowdsourced, and a 'human-transcription-on-demand' tag suggests collection and transcription run as an incremental commissioned pipeline rather than a finished fixed-size release, so the size may not be stable. At this scale and under a non-commercial licence it is an evaluation set or a fine-tuning increment, not a training corpus on its own.
igbo_relevance: Monolingual Igbo audio with human transcripts is scarce enough that even a sub-1k-clip set earns its place, most usefully as a held-out test set for the Nigerian-multilingual Whisper checkpoints already tracked here, where Igbo error rates are otherwise buried in a five-variety aggregate; before adopting it, verify whether the transcripts carry tone diacritics and how many distinct speakers and dialects are represented.

title: Development and Evaluation of HEAL, a Bilingual English-Luganda RAG Chatbot for Disease Surveillance in Uganda
summary: A retrieval-augmented chatbot serving public-health disease-surveillance queries in both English and Luganda, from a large and largely Ugandan author group. OpenAlex has indexed no abstract for this preprint, so it is logged as a lead rather than a summarised result; the parts worth reading are how a retrieval corpus that is almost certainly English-only is made to answer in a low-resource Bantu language, and whether the evaluation measures Luganda generation quality directly or only scores the English path and assumes translation is lossless.
igbo_relevance: An English knowledge base behind a local-language conversational interface is the most plausible near-term deployment shape for Igbo LLM work, and published African-language instances that include an evaluation component at all are rare, so this is worth reading specifically for how they assessed answer quality in a language with no reference QA set.

title: Beyond Native Norms: Decolonizing AI Speech Recognition for Accent Equity in Nigerian ESL Classrooms
summary: Synthesises the second-language speech and World Englishes literature to argue that commercial ASR treats educated Nigerian English as defective rather than as a legitimate variety, citing 20% to over 40% higher error rates on non-native, regional, and Outer Circle Englishes than on Inner Circle benchmarks. The proposal is pedagogical rather than technical: an 'eco-contextual' model in which ASR feedback is mediated by a teacher and validated sociolinguistically instead of being taken as ground truth about pronunciation. No system is built or measured here and the error-rate figures come from prior work, so the operative contribution is the argument that open African-accented speech corpora are the prerequisite for fixing the underlying bias.
igbo_relevance: Igbo-accented Nigerian English is the code-switching partner in most naturally occurring Igbo speech, so an ASR system that penalises it will also fail on the English spans inside otherwise Igbo recordings; the paper is most useful as a framing for why per-variety error reporting and locally recorded evaluation audio matter more than a headline WER.

title: An NLP Tool for Translating Welfare Information: A Hybrid Controlled-Language and Domain-Adapted NMT Approach
summary: Describes a deployed pipeline for rendering legalistic public-benefits documents into plain target-language text, combining enforcement of a controlled source register, domain-adapted NMT, rule-based validation of the numerals and eligibility conditions that carry the most risk, and human review on high-stakes passages. Evaluation is task-based rather than BLEU-based, scoring whether users could complete a benefits task and how often high-risk errors survived, with reported gains over off-the-shelf MT on both. The chapter is thin on specifics (no language inventory, base model, or dataset sizes appear in the abstract), so it is logged for the pipeline design and evaluation framing rather than for reproducible numbers.
igbo_relevance: Constraining the source register before translating and then validating the output against rules is a cheap route to Igbo MT that is safe enough for government and health communication long before general-purpose quality arrives, and a task-completion metric fits Igbo better than BLEU, where references are scarce and orthographic disagreement depresses surface-overlap scores independently of meaning.

title: Automatic transformation of Kazakh text into sign language glosses using multilingual transformer-based models
summary: Builds an 11,190-pair Kazakh text-to-gloss dataset from educational material and fine-tunes mT5-small and mT5-base on it, reporting that the larger model gains roughly 2.6 BLEU (87.5 to 90.1) along with better morphological handling and token coverage. The absolute scores are high enough to suggest the gloss mapping is close to deterministic, so the headline numbers say more about the task than the method; what is worth having is the controlled small-versus-base comparison at about ten thousand pairs, which is the data regime most Igbo sequence-to-sequence work sits in.
igbo_relevance: A borderline keep, retained for the data-regime finding rather than the language or the task, namely that at roughly ten thousand pairs capacity rather than data is still the binding constraint, which argues against defaulting to the smallest multilingual checkpoint when fine-tuning Igbo MT; the morphological error analysis is a secondary draw given Igbo's agglutinative verb complexes.

title: Automatic speech recognition system for court proceedings in Ethiopia
summary: OpenAlex has indexed no abstract for this preprint, so it is logged as a lead rather than a summarised result. The title indicates a domain-specific ASR system built for legal/court-proceeding transcription in an Ethiopian language, a register with strict terminology and formal syntax that stresses systems trained mainly on conversational speech; which language, architecture, and error rates are used remain to be read off the full text.
igbo_relevance: Domain-adapted ASR for a specialised, high-stakes register in an under-resourced African-language setting is a template worth reading before scoping any Igbo court-transcription or public-service ASR effort, where register mismatch is likely a bigger obstacle than raw audio scarcity.

title: Improving Speech Recognition for Ghanaian Accents Using Transformer-Based Accent Classification
summary: OpenAlex has indexed no abstract for this record, so it is logged as a lead rather than a summarised result. The title indicates a transformer-based accent-classification module used to condition or route ASR for Ghanaian-accented speech, the kind of auxiliary task used to close the error-rate gap that non-standard accents suffer on models tuned to inner-circle varieties.
igbo_relevance: Accent classification as a conditioning signal for ASR is a plausible substitute for scarce dialect-labelled Igbo training data, since Igbo speakers carry regional accents into both Igbo and English speech and a single aggregate model is likely to underserve some of them.

title: Digital inclusion and sustainable language preservation: Examining Wikipedia as a tool for social equity through Setswana and Ha Nhi language communities
summary: A mixed-methods study combining interviews with Wikipedia editors, language activists, and digital-literacy educators with platform metrics (article counts, active-editor figures, content growth) across Setswana speakers in South Africa and the Ha Nhi minority in Vietnam. Both communities show constrained digital participation driven by structurally distinct but convergent barriers - infrastructural inequity, editorial gatekeeping, and procedural governance - which the authors frame as "platform-induced hermeneutical injustice," extending existing digital-inclusion models.
igbo_relevance: Names concrete, actionable barriers (editor gatekeeping, governance procedures, infrastructure gaps) to growing an African language's presence on Wikipedia and similar open platforms, directly relevant to planning Igbo-language corpus growth and community outreach on the same platforms.

title: Nwada1/igbo-yoruba-proverb-afriteva
summary: A T5-architecture checkpoint (the name suggests an AfriTeVA base) fine-tuned on paired Igbo and Yoruba proverbs. The model card was not reachable from this environment and downloads are at zero, so whether the task is translation between the two proverb sets, generation, or paraphrase/explanation is unconfirmed from the catalogue metadata alone.
igbo_relevance: Proverbs are a dense, culturally loaded genre that generic MT and LLM systems handle badly, so a purpose-built Igbo-Yoruba proverb model is worth checking as a possible source of parallel proverb data or a baseline for figurative-language evaluation, once the actual task and training data are confirmed from the model card.

title: PeaceMmesoma-15/Igbo-qwen-finetuned
summary: A Qwen-family checkpoint fine-tuned on Igbo, published with no dataset card, training details, or downloads, so the parameter count, fine-tuning data, and intended task (instruction-following, generation, or translation) cannot be confirmed from the catalogue alone.
igbo_relevance: One of very few open Igbo LLM fine-tunes on the hub, worth a quick capability check against existing Igbo LLM baselines before deciding whether the training recipe or data source is worth requesting from the author.

title: Kasaba6330/yoruba-naija-svc-benchmark
summary: A sub-1,000-example benchmark tagged with image-folder format and image modality despite the "svc" label, which most plausibly reads as a voice-conversion benchmark given the Yoruba/Naija framing; the mismatch between the name and the declared image modality needs checking against the actual repo contents before drawing any conclusion.
igbo_relevance: Flagged for the naming inconsistency alone, since a genuine Yoruba/Pidgin voice-conversion benchmark would be directly reusable as an evaluation template for Igbo accent-normalisation or voice-conversion work if the modality tag turns out to be wrong and audio is actually present.

title: AdaobiU/ada_igbo_literacy_dataset
summary: A small (under 1,000 rows) single-file CSV dataset targeting Igbo literacy; no further description is available from the catalogue metadata, but the size and format suggest reading-practice sentences or vocabulary lists rather than a large annotated corpus.
igbo_relevance: Igbo-specific by construction, and literacy material of this kind is a plausible source of clean, simple-register sentences for bootstrapping tokenisers or as easy-mode evaluation examples, worth a direct look at the CSV before use.

title: Khaycee/adaption-igbo-biblical-texts
summary: A 1K-10K-row JSON dataset framed for instruction-tuning on biblical text, titled as an Igbo adaptation but carrying Hugging Face language tags for Vietnamese, English, and "multilingual" rather than Igbo, a mismatch between the title and the declared metadata that should be resolved before use.
igbo_relevance: Biblical text is one of the largest sources of parallel, professionally translated Igbo text and a long-standing pretraining source for Igbo NLP, but the title/metadata mismatch here means the actual language of the text needs verifying before treating it as usable Igbo data.

title: Mixtex: Data-Efficient Latex OCR Via Synthetic Pretraining and Limited Fine-Tuning
summary: Trains a LaTeX-OCR model entirely on synthetic pairs of grammatical Wikipedia text glued to LaTeX formulas rather than real scanned documents, building 120M synthetic tokens before spending only 400 real annotated samples on adaptation. The two-stage recipe outperforms baselines trained on large real datasets on a mixed printed and handwritten English/Chinese benchmark while needing far less human annotation effort.
igbo_relevance: Kept for the general recipe rather than the OCR task itself, since generating large amounts of cheap synthetic paired data and reserving only a few hundred real examples for adaptation is the same strategy an Igbo print-digitisation or diacritic-restoration pipeline needs, given how little real annotated Igbo OCR ground truth exists.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in African Historiography: Augmenting Historical Sources
summary: A conceptual, mixed-methods survey arguing AI can complement rather than replace traditional African historiographical methods, citing speech recognition for transcribing oral tradition, machine learning for deciphering ancient manuscripts and Ajami texts, and computational linguistics for surfacing relationships embedded in African languages. No system is built or benchmarked, so it functions as a scoping argument rather than a technical contribution.
igbo_relevance: Names oral-tradition transcription and manuscript decipherment as concrete AI-assisted entry points into undigitised African-language heritage material, which maps directly onto the Igbo oral-history and mission-era-text corpus-acquisition problem this project already tracks, even though the paper itself offers no method to adopt.

title: Khaycee/adaption-igbo-biblical-texts
summary: A small (1K-10K row) instruction-tuning style dataset of biblical/family-themed text adapted into Igbo. The card's own language and multilinguality tags list Vietnamese and multilingual alongside Igbo despite the Igbo-specific title, suggesting stale template metadata or an unclean mixed-language file.
igbo_relevance: A direct Igbo-language corpus resource, but the tag mismatch should be checked against actual file contents before treating it as clean monolingual Igbo text.

title: AdaobiU/ada_igbo_literacy_dataset
summary: A newly published Igbo literacy dataset with almost no card metadata yet (no size, split, or task tags, zero downloads), likely early-stage educational material paired with the adapter model from the same author.
igbo_relevance: A direct-language resource worth revisiting once the card is filled in, to check size and novelty relative to existing literacy/educational Igbo text.

title: AdaobiU/ada_igbo_literacy_adapter
summary: A lightweight adapter (LoRA-style, by naming) released alongside the literacy dataset from the same author, presumably fine-tuned for an Igbo literacy or reading task; no further description on the card yet.
igbo_relevance: A data point on adapter-based fine-tuning for Igbo-specific tasks, worth a follow-up once base model and evaluation details are documented.

title: Poly-Dialectal Neural Machine Translation System for Bangla Regional Dialects
summary: Builds a unified multi-directional NMT system across 12 Bangla regional dialects translating dialect-to-dialect directly rather than via a standard pivot, backed by a new 51,531-pair multi-dialect parallel corpus including 2,500 expert-verified pairs for five previously uncovered dialects. Fine-tuning BanglaT5 with DoRA beats NLLB-200 and mBART-50, with a scaling study reporting data thresholds for adapting to a new low-resource dialect.
igbo_relevance: The parameter-efficient DoRA recipe and dialect-scaling thresholds transfer directly to modelling Igbo's own dialect continuum without forcing translation through a single standard-Igbo pivot.

title: When the Knowledge Base Becomes the Gold Standard: Measuring Resource-Shared Evaluation Loops in Entity-Level Machine Translation
summary: Shows that when the same knowledge base used to inject correct name translations also sources the gold evaluation set, measured quality gains largely reflect KB agreement rather than genuine translation improvement; gains vanish outside the KB-overlapping portion of an independently annotated test set.
igbo_relevance: A direct warning for Igbo NER/MT evaluation leaning on gazetteers or knowledge bases as both a translation aid and the gold standard, since the same contamination could inflate reported gains.

title: Between accuracy and empathy: A comparative study of human and transformer-based multi-label emotion annotation
summary: Compares four approaches to multi-label emotion annotation on a 408-narrative Serbian corpus against the GoEmotions taxonomy: zero-shot English on machine-translated text, a domain-adapted model fine-tuned on translated data, multilingual XLM-R under hard/soft labels, and regional South-Slavic models. Domain-adapted fine-tuning on translated data beat zero-shot transfer, and a regionally pretrained model outperformed generic multilingual checkpoints.
igbo_relevance: Supports translate-then-fine-tune over zero-shot transfer, and a regionally pretrained multilingual model (AfriBERTa/AfroXLMR for Igbo) over a generic multilingual checkpoint, for Igbo sentiment/emotion work.

title: voicedata/new-naijavoices-kanitts2-tokenized
summary: A speech dataset from the NaijaVoices namespace, pre-tokenized for the KaniTTS2 architecture per its name. The catalogue exposes only a region:us tag and zero downloads, so the covered Nigerian language(s) cannot be confirmed without opening the repo.
igbo_relevance: The NaijaVoices project has previously spanned multiple Nigerian languages, so this KaniTTS2-tokenized release is worth a direct check for an Igbo split before treating it as usable TTS training data.

title: Iterative Self-Learning for Expressive Text-to-Speech Synthesis
summary: Proposes an iterative self-learning framework that recovers discrete expressive labels (word-level prominence, utterance-level emotion) by inverting a frozen generative model, then repeatedly pseudo-labels unlabeled speech and retrains on the combined labeled and pseudo-labeled set. Across several low-resource data splits, iterative refinement beats single-pass pseudo-labeling and approaches fully supervised quality in the most label-scarce conditions.
igbo_relevance: Expressive and prosodic labels are exactly the annotation Igbo TTS lacks at scale given tone's role in the language, so this self-learning recipe is a plausible way to bootstrap expressive/tone labels from mostly unlabeled Igbo speech.

title: An AI-Based Adaptive Learning Platform for Multilingual and Low-Resource Educational Contexts: A Case Study on Nigeria
summary: Builds an adaptive-learning platform case-studied on Nigerian Pidgin English, curating a Pidgin corpus to fine-tune an instruction-tuned LLM and comparing 4-, 5-, and 8-bit quantisation for the trade-off between semantic fidelity and inference cost, validated by native-speaker cultural assessment.
igbo_relevance: The pairing of a curated low-resource corpus, instruction fine-tuning, a quantisation trade-off study, and native-speaker cultural evaluation is a reusable blueprint for an Igbo-language instructional LLM deployment.

title: voicedata/naijavoices_yoruba_nanocodec
summary: A Yoruba-language speech dataset from the NaijaVoices project, tokenised with a nanocodec representation for downstream TTS or codec-based modelling; sized in the 100K-1M row range and distributed as parquet, with no further license or audio detail exposed in the catalogue.
igbo_relevance: Yoruba is a fellow Nigerian language and a natural cross-lingual proxy for Igbo speech modelling, so if the same nanocodec pipeline is later applied to Igbo, this dataset's structure and tooling would transfer directly.

title: Africanvoice/African_voices_igbo
summary: An Igbo-specific speech dataset released alongside a companion Naija-voices set from the same namespace; the catalogue exposes almost no metadata beyond a region tag, so scale and audio quality are unconfirmed without opening the repo.
igbo_relevance: A direct Igbo speech resource worth a hands-on check for size and quality before use in ASR/TTS training.

title: Africanvoice/African_voices_naija
summary: A 100K-1M row audio-plus-text dataset distributed as parquet, matched on the naija query; the specific Nigerian language(s) covered are not stated in the catalogue tags.
igbo_relevance: Released from the same namespace as an explicit Igbo-labelled sibling dataset, so worth checking whether this larger release also contains an Igbo split.

title: Professor/igbo-speech-data
summary: A newly listed Igbo speech dataset with no descriptive metadata beyond a region tag and zero recorded downloads, so size, format, and recording conditions are unknown from the catalogue alone.
igbo_relevance: Igbo-specific by construction; worth a follow-up look once the card is populated.

title: Bridging context gaps in low-resource language chatbots through multilevel attention and hybrid embedding approaches
source: Journal of the Nigerian Society of Physical Sciences
summary: Combines FastText subword vectors with mBERT and hierarchical word/utterance/dialogue-level attention to build an Igbo-English conversational agent resistant to context drift and code-switching noise, benchmarked against LSTM, Transformer, FastText, mBERT, and XLM-R baselines with strong BLEU/ROUGE-L/context-retention/intent-F1 results and positive human evaluation.
igbo_relevance: An Igbo-specific dialogue architecture and evaluation suite directly reusable as a baseline or benchmark for Igbo conversational-AI work.

title: Democratizing Machine Translation: A CPU-Centric Training Pipeline for Low-Resource Languages (A Kalabari Case Study)
source: International Journal of Computer Science and Mathematical Theory
summary: Builds a from-scratch NMT system for Kalabari, a Niger-Congo Ijo-family language of Nigeria, using a manually assembled 10,222-pair parallel corpus and a lightweight Transformer trained entirely on consumer CPU hardware, then served with INT8 quantisation via CTranslate2.
igbo_relevance: A reproducible, GPU-free NMT training and deployment recipe from another low-resource Nigerian Niger-Congo language, directly adaptable for Igbo MT development in compute-constrained settings.

title: Distinguishing lexical deviation from semantic resilience in LLM-based round-trip translation
summary: Runs 80,000 round-trip translation operations across four systems and multiple metrics, showing outputs stay fluent while meaning degrades quickly and surface-overlap metrics mask this loss, a surface fidelity trap that also exposes metric mismatches for paraphrase evaluation.
igbo_relevance: A direct caution against relying on round-trip translation for Igbo MT or paraphrase data augmentation without an independent, paraphrase-aware quality check.

title: Benchmarking retrieval augmented generation LLMs for Arabic noise robustness
summary: Builds a 300-question, 6,196-document Arabic RAG benchmark testing noise robustness and negative rejection across six multilingual LLMs, finding consistent degradation under noisy retrieval and frequent over-cautious refusal errors.
igbo_relevance: No comparable RAG robustness benchmark exists for Igbo; this noise-robustness and negative-rejection evaluation methodology could be directly repurposed for a future Igbo-language RAG system.

title: Toadoum/naija-tts
summary: A multilingual Nigerian voice-cloning/TTS checkpoint fine-tuned from ResembleAI's Chatterbox base, with explicit language tags for Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, and Nigerian English, but no card detail on training data size, voice count, or audio quality.
igbo_relevance: An Igbo-tagged open TTS/voice-cloning model worth a direct listen-test against existing Igbo TTS baselines before adoption.

title: TranslatePsy-AfriSLM: High-Quality Data Scaling For Low-Resource Machine Translation
summary: Releases an open MT resource collection spanning 19 Sub-Saharan African languages: curated parallel data, African-specialised synthetic data, and a family of fine-tuned small language models. Unified quality-estimation filtering discards up to 96% of training tokens without hurting quality, filtered synthetic data dominates the quality-efficiency Pareto frontier, and the resulting sub-1B-parameter models outperform much larger general MT systems.
igbo_relevance: Whether Igbo is among the 19 languages is unconfirmed from the abstract, but the QE-filtering and synthetic-data scaling recipe is directly transferable to building an efficient, small Igbo MT system regardless.

title: Structure, Association, and Decision Value: Representation-Based Difficulty Estimation for Adaptive Inference in African-Language NLI
languages: 15 African languages via AfriXNLI, unspecified list
summary: Tests whether internal representation statistics (angular dispersion, effective rank) from frozen multilingual checkpoints can serve as difficulty signals for adaptive-inference routing on NLI across 15 African languages, finding none of the tested signals beat always-expensive inference. Also reports that AfriXNLI's English, French, and Swahili configurations share the bulk of their examples verbatim with XNLI, so they cannot cleanly evaluate XNLI-trained models.
igbo_relevance: Whether Igbo is among the 15 evaluated languages is unconfirmed, but the negative finding on representation-based difficulty routing and the contamination warning for XNLI-derived benchmarks are directly applicable cautions for any future Igbo NLI evaluation or model-routing setup.

title: CodeWithSiya/afriberta-large-cpt-xho
summary: An AfriBERTa-large checkpoint continued-pretrained on Xhosa data (XLM-RoBERTa architecture per its tags), published with no card detail on corpus size or training procedure beyond the naming convention.
igbo_relevance: AfriBERTa's original multilingual pretraining corpus already includes Igbo, so this continued-pretraining recipe for specialising the shared backbone to one African language is a directly transferable technique for boosting Igbo-specific performance from the same base model.

title: iamwille/igbo-tts-speecht5-processed-v3
summary: A processed Igbo TTS dataset packaged for SpeechT5 fine-tuning, distributed as parquet with 10K-100K rows. It is the third same-day reprocessing pass from this author, with no card detail yet on audio source, speaker count, or licensing.
igbo_relevance: Direct Igbo TTS training data pre-formatted for a common fine-tuning target (SpeechT5), worth a hands-on check of alignment quality and licence before adoption.

title: A Speech Corpus for Mizo Automatic Speech Recognition: Whisper and SraVaani 1.0 Fine-Tuning with Morphology-Aware Evaluation
summary: Builds a Mizo ASR system from 17.62 hours of curated speech, fine-tuning three Whisper variants and the SraVaani 1.0 Indic multilingual model, scoring results with both conventional WER and a new morphology-aware WER; Whisper-large-v3 reaches 18.08% conventional WER (7.22% morphology-aware), and SraVaani improves from 58.27% zero-shot to 29.45% (17.93% morphology-aware) after fine-tuning.
igbo_relevance: Mizo is tonal and morphologically rich like Igbo, so both the Whisper-adaptation recipe for an unseen tonal language and the morphology-aware WER metric are directly transferable to Igbo ASR training and evaluation.

title: The Geometry of Low-Resource Language Representations
languages: 30 languages studied, 10 African languages for CPT experiments, unspecified list
summary: Characterises the performance gap between low- and high-resource languages inside LLMs through representational geometry, finding systematic representational degeneration in final layers for low-resource languages. Geometric regularisation during continued pretraining across 9 base LLMs adapted to 10 African languages reduces this degeneration and gives small but consistent gains on the hardest tasks for larger models.
igbo_relevance: If Igbo is among the adapted languages this gives a diagnostic and a concrete CPT fix for continue-pretraining a general LLM on Igbo text; even if not, the diagnostic and regulariser are architecture-level and should transfer directly.

title: Unsupervised Speech Recognition at the Syllable Level
languages: English benchmarks, generalisation claim for low-resource languages, unspecified list
summary: Proposes a syllable-level unsupervised ASR framework based on masked language modelling, avoiding the grapheme-to-phoneme converters phone-level UASR needs and the training instability of GAN-based UASR objectives. Reports up to 40% relative CER reduction on LibriSpeech and better generalisation than prior phone-level approaches on languages with ambiguous phoneme boundaries.
igbo_relevance: Igbo orthography often drops tone diacritics while syllable boundaries stay stable, so a syllable-level UASR objective is a plausible route to bootstrapping ASR from unpaired Igbo speech and text without building a G2P converter first.

title: JohnAlbarkaIbrahim/afroxlmr-mini-nigerian-sentiment
summary: An AfroXLMR-mini checkpoint fine-tuned for sentiment classification across the major Nigerian language varieties plus English, released with an int8 ONNX export and tagged for WhatsApp-style informal text. No benchmark numbers are visible from the listing itself.
igbo_relevance: A directly usable Igbo sentiment baseline built on an Africa-focused encoder, worth benchmarking against AfriBERTa-based alternatives on held-out Igbo text before adoption.

title: Bayesian optimization for data selection in multilingual neural machine translation
summary: OpenAlex has not indexed an abstract for this record, so it is logged as a lead: the title indicates a Bayesian-optimisation approach to choosing which multilingual data to train on for NMT, a data-efficiency method rather than a resource release.
igbo_relevance: Principled data selection is exactly the lever available for Igbo MT, where parallel data is scarce and the composition of the multilingual mix it is trained alongside likely matters more than raw volume.
